ENFJ>INTJ.title: You work out plans for everyone, on your own.
ENFJ>INTJ.body: When a friend comes to you with a problem, you listen first, then help them sort it out step by step: "Okay, so what if you tried this?" Once a trip is decided, you put together ideas for where to go and a budget that same day and send them to everyone. You like meeting people, but you also value time to think alone.
ENFJ>INTJ.say: "I've worked out the flow. Tell me if anything doesn't work for you."
ENFJ>INTJ.do: When choosing where to move, you pick a neighborhood by thinking about your life five years from now.
ENFJ>INTJ.do_s: When choosing a club, you think about what your time will look like all the way until graduation.
ENFJ>INTJ.worry: Even with a faster way to get things done, you worry someone might feel bad, and you can't decide. The gap between days you want people and days you don't is big, and it throws you off too.
ENFJ>INTJ.karai: Once a trip is booked, you learn so much about the local restaurants that it feels like you've already been.
ENFJ>INTJ.aru: When you're in charge of a welcome party, the prep is really fun. But on the day, as your turn for the toast gets closer, you suddenly want to go home.
ENFJ>INTJ.aru_s: When you're in charge of your club's welcome party for new members, the prep is really fun. But on the day, as your turn to give the opening speech gets closer, you suddenly want to go home.
ENFJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and decides with your feelings. As you gained experience, you became able to think things through alone and decide with logic. Your love of thinking ahead and preparing is the same as ever. You can enjoy the prep because you can do it while thinking on your own, but a toast in front of a big group uses up a lot of energy all at once, so as that moment gets closer, you want to go home.
ENFJ>INTJ.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself in a meeting or picture yourself with friends, and your result can change.
ENFJ>INTJ.yure_s: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself planning a group presentation or picture yourself with friends, and your result can change.
ENFJ>INTJ.plus: You hesitate over efficient plans because you picture the people who might get left behind. Your plans take everyone into account, so people feel safe with them.
ENFJ>INTJ.tip: When you share a plan, leave one part as "Let's decide this together." You don't have to decide it all alone, so it's easier to make up your mind.
ENFJ>INTJ.hidden: You often think with logic, but you were born good at noticing small changes in how people feel. When someone's voice gets a little quieter in a meeting, don't you right away ask, "What do you think?" Use that, and people will happily get on board with your plans.
ENFJ>INTJ.hidden_s: You often think with logic, but you were born good at noticing small changes in how people feel. When someone's voice gets a little quieter during a group discussion, don't you right away ask, "What do you think?" Use that, and people will happily get on board with your plans.

ENFJ>INTP.title: You listen, and end up sorting out the cause too.
ENFJ>INTP.body: While looking at paintings in a museum, you're wondering, "What was the person who painted this feeling?" When a painter catches your interest, you start looking up stories from their younger days on the train home. After talking with people, you also want time to think alone.
ENFJ>INTP.say: "Wouldn't it be amazing if that actually worked?"
ENFJ>INTP.do: You look something up on your phone, and before you know it you're reading about something else entirely.
ENFJ>INTP.worry: You want to help people, and you also want to think about what interests you, so you're never sure how to spend your time. You can't move until your thoughts come together, but you keep thinking about the people you're keeping waiting.
ENFJ>INTP.karai: One news story, and you're worrying about things years down the road.
ENFJ>INTP.aru: When a friend says "I want to quit my part-time job," you listen, and somehow you're asking "What's the worst part?" and digging out the reasons. Even though you really want to cheer them up.
ENFJ>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people, decides with your feelings, and wants things to go as planned. Through all kinds of experiences, you also became able to get lost in thought alone, check things with logic, and wait and see without deciding. Your wish to cheer people up hasn't gone away. When you hear a friend's problem, you want to pin down what's causing it before you cheer them up, so the questions come out of your mouth first.
ENFJ>INTP.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. The question "Do you like to plan things out?" especially can flip depending on whether you picture yourself before a deadline or on a day off.
ENFJ>INTP.plus: Advice turns into looking for the cause because you really want to solve their problem. Having someone think it through with them makes people feel supported.
ENFJ>INTP.tip: Before you talk about the cause, first just say, "That sounds really hard." After that, your thoughts will actually help them.
ENFJ>INTP.hidden: You often go with the flow, but you were also born good at getting ready ahead of time. The day before a trip, don't you check your bag again and again for anything you forgot? Use that for important plans and work, and people will feel safe leaving things to you.
ENFJ>INTP.hidden_s: You often go with the flow, but you were also born good at getting ready ahead of time. The day before a trip, don't you check your bag again and again for anything you forgot? Use that for important plans and assignments, and people will feel safe leaving things to you.

ENFJ>ENTJ.title: You decide firmly, then quietly check on people.
ENFJ>ENTJ.body: You set goals and lead everyone forward, and when someone can't keep up, you go over and check on them. In meetings you assign roles right there, "Okay, this by next week," and afterward you go around asking each person, "Does that seem doable?" You decide firmly with logic, but later you also worry about how the other person feels.
ENFJ>ENTJ.say: "How about the first Saturday of next month for the next meetup?"
ENFJ>ENTJ.do: On a trip with friends, you settle everything from where to go to the train home, right there with everyone.
ENFJ>ENTJ.worry: Even when you made the right call, at night you go over whether anyone got hurt. Even when you should be strict, one look at their face and you soften your words.
ENFJ>ENTJ.karai: Even in idle chat, you end up asking, "So who's doing what?"
ENFJ>ENTJ.aru: At practice with your hobby band, you say firmly, "Learn this song by next time." But on the train home, you remember the new member who answered quietly and wonder whether to send them a message.
ENFJ>ENTJ.aru_s: At club practice you say firmly, "Learn this song by next time." But on the train home, you remember the first-year who answered quietly and wonder whether to send them a message.
ENFJ>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who decides with your feelings. As you gained experience, you became able to decide based on "What will move us forward?" rather than the mood in the room. Still, worrying about how the other person took it is still clearly there. When you speak, you can say it with moving forward in mind, but once you settle down on the way home, the new member's quiet reply bugs you, and you go back and forth on whether to text them.
ENFJ>ENTJ.why_s: By birth, you're the type who decides with your feelings. As you grew up, you became able to decide based on "What will move practice forward?" rather than the mood in the room. Still, worrying about how the other person took it is still clearly there. During practice you can speak firmly, but once you settle down on the way home, a first-year's quiet reply bugs you, and you go back and forth on whether to text them.
ENFJ>ENTJ.yure: The only difference is logic or feelings. Picture yourself making a call at work and you lean toward logic. Picture a friend asking for advice and you lean toward feelings.
ENFJ>ENTJ.yure_s: The only difference is logic or feelings. Picture yourself making a decision for your club or class and you lean toward logic. Picture a friend asking for advice and you lean toward feelings.
ENFJ>ENTJ.plus: You remember their face after deciding because you really pay attention to people. That's why people trust you even when you're strict.
ENFJ>ENTJ.tip: On days you say something strict, send a message that same day: "Sorry if I was too much. You always help so much." It clears your mind so you don't lie awake thinking about it.
ENFJ>ENTJ.hidden: You often decide with logic, but you were born good at noticing feelings people don't say. Don't you sometimes hear a friend's "I'm fine" and know from their voice they're actually tired? Use that, and people will feel really understood.

ENFJ>ENTP.title: You come up with fun ideas and get everyone on board.
ENFJ>ENTP.body: In discussions, you say, "What if we think about it backward?" and come up with an idea no one else thought of. And you shape it into something everyone can get on board with. You keep building on topics someone brings up, and before you know it, everyone is talking. When something seems off, you point it out with a laugh.
ENFJ>ENTP.say: "Let's hear from the people who disagree, too."
ENFJ>ENTP.do: Chatting over dinner, you say "Let's all do this sometime!" and make a group chat right then.
ENFJ>ENTP.worry: You want to push your idea forward, but you also understand how the people against it feel, so you can't bring it up. Right after you make a plan, a more fun way pops up and you can't settle.
ENFJ>ENTP.karai: After shooting down someone's idea, you message them, "It was a good idea though."
ENFJ>ENTP.aru: Right after you make a careful trip plan and send it to everyone, you're the one saying, "Actually, wouldn't this route be more fun?"
ENFJ>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type who decides with your feelings and wants a plan made ahead to feel at ease. Through all kinds of experiences, you became able to poke at things with logic and quickly head toward whatever's more fun. You still feel relieved when you make a plan, but your wish to stick to it exactly is weaker than before. Once you've put a plan into shape and sent it, the part of you that reviews things kicks in, and you end up finding a more fun route yourself.
ENFJ>ENTP.yure: The two differences are logic or feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself at a well-prepared event or picture yourself chatting with friends, and your result can change.
ENFJ>ENTP.plus: You want to change ideas because you always believe "We can make this more fun." That positive attitude has helped the people around you many times.
ENFJ>ENTP.tip: Before sending a plan to everyone, sleep on it for one night. If the new idea is good, it'll still be there in the morning, and you'll change plans after sending them less often.
ENFJ>ENTP.hidden: You're great at sharp comebacks, but you were also born good at knowing the words someone most needs to hear. When a friend is down, don't you say "You worked so hard" before you even think? Add a line like that in discussions, and even people who disagreed will listen to you.

ENFJ>INFJ.title: One-on-one, you really listen.
ENFJ>INFJ.body: In front of everyone you cheer people on brightly, and one-on-one you listen closely. Sometimes you name exactly what someone is feeling: "Didn't that make you feel lonely?" The day after you hear someone out, you send a short message: "How's it going since then?"
ENFJ>INFJ.say: "Before we all talk, tell me what you think first."
ENFJ>INFJ.do: The day before an important talk, you think about how the other person feels and decide what order to say things in.
ENFJ>INFJ.worry: The more you helped people that day, the more drained you are when you get home. You take in people's worries so deeply that your own heart gets heavy too.
ENFJ>INFJ.karai: You pick a friend's birthday present a month ahead, then keep wondering "Is this really right?" until the day.
ENFJ>INFJ.aru: You go out to eat with friends you haven't seen in a while, nodding and laughing along. On the way home you're suddenly exhausted, and even in bed you're still thinking about the worries you heard.
ENFJ>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energized by being with people. As the years went by, you came to rest your feelings with time alone. Taking in people's worries as if they were your own has been the same since way back. Even after using up your energy among people, the worries you heard stay in your heart, so even though you're worn out on the way home, you keep thinking about them after you get into bed.
ENFJ>INFJ.yure: The only difference is whether people energize you or you recharge alone. Picture your weekend or picture the day of a big get-together, and your result can change.
ENFJ>INFJ.plus: You're drained on the way home because you really listened to everyone there. Talking with people without holding back is one of your best qualities.
ENFJ>INFJ.tip: On days you see people, take 30 minutes after you get home to put your phone down and do nothing. Rest your body first, and you'll have energy to listen again.
ENFJ>INFJ.hidden: You value time alone to think, but you were born good at sorting out your thoughts by talking. Haven't you found the answer yourself while telling a friend about a worry? When you're stuck, talk to someone instead of carrying it alone, and you'll decide faster.

ENFJ>INFP.title: For other people, you move right away.
ENFJ>INFP.body: You move right away for someone else, but when it comes to yourself, you think it over carefully until you feel, "This is it." When you hear a friend is feeling down, you go see them that same day with their favorite snack. You like being with people, but you also need time alone to sort out your feelings.
ENFJ>INFP.say: "I get how you feel. You can answer later, okay?"
ENFJ>INFP.do: Listening to a favorite song, you imagine, "Maybe this is about a breakup."
ENFJ>INFP.worry: You want to meet people's expectations, but if it's something you don't want to do, you can't get going. Even with a plan, on days you're not in the mood you can't get started, and then you blame yourself.
ENFJ>INFP.karai: Just the movie trailer has you tearing up.
ENFJ>INFP.aru: When a friend changes jobs, you cheer them on with everything: "You've got this!" But your own class sign-up page has been sitting open for a week.
ENFJ>INFP.aru_s: When a friend has a big game or competition, you cheer them on with everything: "You've got this!" But your own class sign-up page has been sitting open for a week.
ENFJ>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and sets up a plan before acting. As you gained experience, you came to check your feelings alone and act according to the moment. You can still put together plans for other people right away, just like before. When it comes to yourself, you can't decide until you've checked in your heart, "Do I really want to do this?", so your hands stop with the sign-up page still open.
ENFJ>INFP.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself helping someone or picture a day off alone, and your result can change.
ENFJ>INFP.plus: You hesitate about your own things because you don't want to do what you're not sure about. Once you decide to do it, you can really put your heart into it.
ENFJ>INFP.tip: Tell a close friend in one line what you want to do. They'll ask "How's that going?", and it'll be easier to take the first step.
ENFJ>INFP.hidden: You like quiet time checking in with your feelings, but you were also born good at brightening a room. At a new get-together, don't you find yourself introducing people who don't know each other? Use that, and you'll fit in fast at a new job or class.
ENFJ>INFP.hidden_s: You like quiet time checking in with your feelings, but you were also born good at brightening a room. At a new get-together, don't you find yourself introducing people who don't know each other? Use that, and you'll fit in fast in a new class or club.

ENFJ>ENFJ.title: When you say "You've got this," you mean it.
ENFJ>ENFJ.body: When you say, "Don't worry, you can do it," you truly mean it. When you hear a friend is starting something new, you're the first to say, "That's great!" and you might even introduce them to someone who could help. You feel free in places where people count on you, but when days of working quietly alone go on, you tend to lose your energy.
ENFJ>ENFJ.say: "It's okay, you can do this. Let's do it together!"
ENFJ>ENFJ.do: At a get-together full of strangers, you introduce people to each other, and by the time you leave you've made a group chat.
ENFJ>ENFJ.worry: When people ask, you take it all on, and your own time disappears. If the mood around you drops even a little, you wonder if it's your fault.
ENFJ>ENFJ.karai: When a friend asks for love advice, you make a game plan more seriously than they do.
ENFJ>ENFJ.aru: When someone in the group goes quiet, you worry "Did I say something?" and switch to a brighter topic.
ENFJ>ENFJ.why: Your temperament and character are the same combination in all four letters. Getting energy among people and caring about the mood of the room has carried on just as it is since you were a kid. Since it didn't change with experience, this habit shows up strongly. When someone goes quiet in a conversation, you worry they aren't having fun, so you end up switching to a brighter topic.
ENFJ>ENFJ.yure: All four line up, so you tend to get the same result no matter how many times you take it. If you get a different one, you may be carrying too many favors and wanting to be alone more than usual.
ENFJ>ENFJ.plus: You notice changes in the mood right away, so you can reach out to anyone who might be left alone. With you around, everyone feels safe to talk.
ENFJ>ENFJ.tip: When someone goes quiet, pause for a breath before changing the subject. Asking later, "Were you okay back there?" is easier on both of you.
ENFJ>ENFJ.hidden: You're great at sticking to the plan, but you also have a not-yet-used "enjoy the moment" side. Has a shop you wandered into on a day when plans fell apart ever become your best memory? Use that, and you can laugh easily even when things don't go as planned.

ENFJ>ENFP.title: You always leave free time in trip plans.
ENFJ>ENFP.body: You leave a slot in your trip plans on purpose: "Free time here." You note down places a friend said they wanted to go, then casually make sure you pass by them on the day. Even when things don't go as planned, you can still enjoy it.
ENFJ>ENFP.say: "Hey, want to all go to the beach on our next day off?"
ENFJ>ENFP.do: You plan the birthday party carefully, and on the day you jump right into a game someone just made up.
ENFJ>ENFP.worry: You want people to be happy, so you pack the schedule, and then you have no free time for yourself. The gap between days you want order and days you don't want to decide anything throws you off.
ENFJ>ENFP.karai: You call saying "Let's talk for a sec," and it's never just a sec.
ENFJ>ENFP.aru: On a trip with friends, you looked up and saved every place you wanted to go, but on the day you're the first to say, "Want to try that side street?"
ENFJ>ENFP.why: By birth, you're the type who wants to make plans ahead. Through all kinds of experiences, you also learned the fun of going with the moment. Even now, the part of you that can't relax without looking things up is still there. It's precisely because you've done your research and feel at ease that on the day you can head down a street that catches your eye without hesitating.
ENFJ>ENFP.yure: The only difference is sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture work or getting ready and you lean toward planning. Picture having fun and you lean toward going with the flow.
ENFJ>ENFP.yure_s: The only difference is sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture homework or getting ready and you lean toward planning. Picture having fun and you lean toward going with the flow.
ENFJ>ENFP.plus: You pack the schedule because you want everyone to say "That was fun." Someone who enjoys both the prep and the detours is never boring to be with.
ENFJ>ENFP.tip: When you plan a day, decide just half of it and leave the rest open. That open time often turns into the best memory.
ENFJ>ENFP.hidden: You can enjoy going with the flow, but you were born good at finishing things properly. Don't you sometimes find you've wrapped up a task alone after everyone else got bored and stopped? Use that at work, and people will see you as both fun and reliable.
ENFJ>ENFP.hidden_s: You can enjoy going with the flow, but you were born good at finishing things properly. Don't you sometimes find you've wrapped up a task alone after everyone else got bored and stopped? Use that on assignments and group presentations, and people will see you as both fun and reliable.

ENFJ>ISTJ.title: You follow the rules so no one gets stuck.
ENFJ>ISTJ.body: With materials everyone will use, you check them again and again so anyone can understand them before you share them. People often see you as "very organized," but that's because you don't want to cause anyone trouble. You've even made a note of the steps yourself for a newcomer and handed it to them.
ENFJ>ISTJ.body_s: With materials for a group presentation, you check them again and again so anyone can understand them before you share them. People often see you as "very organized," but that's because you don't want to cause anyone trouble. For a friend who was absent, you send photos of that day's notes along with the deadlines for assignments.
ENFJ>ISTJ.say: "Could you have this done by Friday?"
ENFJ>ISTJ.do: Before a trip, you check the weather and train times and send them to everyone.
ENFJ>ISTJ.worry: You want people to follow the rules, but you don't want to blame them, so you struggle with how to point things out. You want to see people, but if you're not ready, you're tired before you even meet.
ENFJ>ISTJ.karai: You arrive ten minutes early and are already messaging the friend who's running late.
ENFJ>ISTJ.aru: Writing a message to tell a junior about a mistake, you reread it again and again to make sure it doesn't sound harsh, and end up rewriting it three times.
ENFJ>ISTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people, imagines what's ahead, and decides with your feelings. As you gained experience, you became able to focus alone and decide based on how things have been done and on logic. Three letters are different, but worrying about the other person's feelings is still as it was when you were born. You have to tell your junior about the mistake correctly, yet you also don't want to get them down, so you keep rewriting until you find a way of saying it that does both.
ENFJ>ISTJ.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself following procedures at work or picture yourself with friends you get along with, and a different type may come up.
ENFJ>ISTJ.yure_s: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself following the steps in a club or committee or picture yourself with friends you get along with, and a different type may come up.
ENFJ>ISTJ.plus: Because you take such care with your words, people think, "If they say so, I'll listen." You're careful about how you say things, so juniors can listen without worry.
ENFJ>ISTJ.tip: When you need to point something out, decide to always send it in this order: what happened, what you'd like, and thanks. It won't sound harsh, so you can send it without rereading it over and over.
ENFJ>ISTJ.hidden: You build on facts one by one, but you were born good at imagining what's ahead. While working, don't you sometimes think, "This could be better if..."? Say it out loud, and people at work will rely on you even more.
ENFJ>ISTJ.hidden_s: You build on facts one by one, but you were born good at imagining what's ahead. While working on something for your club or committee, don't you sometimes think, "This could be better if..."? Say it out loud, and people around you will rely on you even more.

ENFJ>ISFJ.title: You notice right away when someone's not feeling well.
ENFJ>ISFJ.body: That person doesn't like spicy food, and this person had a bit of a cough yesterday. You're someone who naturally remembers things like that. When someone isn't feeling well, you quietly leave throat lozenges or a warm drink on their desk. You're cheerful in front of everyone and pay close attention to people even where no one sees.
ENFJ>ISFJ.say: "You look pale. Why not head home early today?"
ENFJ>ISFJ.do: When you organize a farewell party, you book a place that serves the food the guest of honor once said they loved.
ENFJ>ISFJ.do_s: When you plan a goodbye party for a senior in your club, you bring the snacks they once said they loved.
ENFJ>ISFJ.worry: Doing things for others doesn't bother you, but your own plans always come last. Some days you want to talk about big dreams, but you stop yourself: "I need to be realistic."
ENFJ>ISFJ.karai: You say "Don't worry about me," and you're the one worrying about everyone the most.
ENFJ>ISFJ.aru: You start telling a friend, "Someday I want to open a shop," and halfway through you end it yourself: "Well, it's not realistic though."
ENFJ>ISFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people and imagines what's ahead. As the years went by, you became able to feel settled on your own and started thinking based on past experience too. Your ability to picture your dreams hasn't gone away. Even while you're talking about your dream, the money and time it would take start to come into clear view halfway through, so you end it yourself with, "Well, it's not realistic though."
ENFJ>ISFJ.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and hunches or facts. Picture yourself at a lively celebration or picture yourself doing daily chores and work, and your result can change.
ENFJ>ISFJ.yure_s: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and hunches or facts. Picture yourself at a lively celebration or picture yourself in your everyday classes and club practice, and your result can change.
ENFJ>ISFJ.plus: Even when you talk about your dreams, you also think about what you can actually do. That's why you can move toward what you want, little by little.
ENFJ>ISFJ.tip: Instead of ending your dream talk with "But it's impossible," try ending with "So what could I do first?" When it ends on a positive note, the people listening will share ideas too.
ENFJ>ISFJ.hidden: You value quiet time alone, but you were born good at bringing people together and livening things up. When a friend you haven't seen in a while comes to mind, don't you say, "Want to get together?" Use that, and your circle of people will keep growing.

ENFJ>ESTJ.title: You're strict, but you always give credit.
ENFJ>ESTJ.body: While checking how the work is going, you praise what the team members did well, even small things. You're strict but liked, because you really notice their effort. The day before a deadline, you check first with anyone who seems behind: "Want some help?"
ENFJ>ESTJ.body_s: While checking how the school festival prep is going, you praise what the team members did well, even small things. You're strict but liked, because you really notice their effort. When a group is falling behind on their work, you go over first and ask, "Want some help?"
ENFJ>ESTJ.say: "Let's finish by the end of the month. This team can do it."
ENFJ>ESTJ.do: At work drinks, you set the ending time so everyone can catch the last train.
ENFJ>ESTJ.do_s: At your club's end-of-season party, you set the ending time so nobody gets home too late.
ENFJ>ESTJ.worry: Every time, you're torn between speaking up to someone who breaks the rules and thinking about their feelings. While you're busy getting work done properly, you feel like you've forgotten what you used to want to do.
ENFJ>ESTJ.worry_s: Every time, you're torn between speaking up to someone who breaks the rules and thinking about their feelings. While you're busy getting everything done properly, you feel like you've forgotten what you used to want to do.
ENFJ>ESTJ.karai: You tell everyone "Go home early," but you're the last one to leave.
ENFJ>ESTJ.aru: You can tell a late coworker plainly, "Please be on time," but the whole way home you keep wondering, "Was I too harsh?"
ENFJ>ESTJ.aru_s: You can tell a teammate who was late to practice plainly, "Please be on time," but the whole way home you keep wondering, "Was I too harsh?"
ENFJ>ESTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who imagines dreams ahead and decides with your feelings. Through dealing with all kinds of people, you became able to look at the facts in front of you and decide with logic. You can say clearly that rules are rules, but worrying about the other person's feelings is the same as ever. You can say what needs saying in the moment, but when you think back on the other person's face afterward, you keep wondering whether you said it too harshly.
ENFJ>ESTJ.yure: The two differences are hunches or facts, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself on the job or picture time with people close to you, and your result can change.
ENFJ>ESTJ.yure_s: The two differences are hunches or facts, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself busy with your club or committee or picture time with people close to you, and your result can change.
ENFJ>ESTJ.plus: You worry about how you said it because you're thinking about that person's future too. Even when you're strict, they can tell you're thinking about them.
ENFJ>ESTJ.tip: After pointing something out, end by telling them one thing they did well. It won't end on harsh words, so you'll worry less on the way home.
ENFJ>ESTJ.hidden: You act on the facts in front of you, but you were born good at imagining years ahead. On the way home from work, don't you sometimes get excited thinking, "In a few years I'd like to change how we do this"? Share that with your team, and it'll be easier for everyone to have a goal.
ENFJ>ESTJ.hidden_s: You act on the facts in front of you, but you were born good at imagining years ahead. On the way home from practice, don't you sometimes get excited thinking, "By the time the younger members take over, I'd like to change how we train"? Share that with your club, and it'll be easier for everyone to have a goal.

ENFJ>ESFJ.title: You can't help taking care of everyone.
ENFJ>ESFJ.body: Being useful to people gives you energy. When a friend's birthday is coming up, you decide ahead of time even who will get the cake. After a get-together, you send that day's photos to the people who couldn't come too.
ENFJ>ESFJ.say: "You haven't had lunch yet, right? I got extra rice balls."
ENFJ>ESFJ.do: You volunteer to help run an event at work or in your neighborhood, and on the day you walk around checking that everyone's having fun.
ENFJ>ESFJ.do_s: You volunteer to help run a school event, and on the day you walk around checking that everyone's having fun.
ENFJ>ESFJ.worry: If even one person doesn't look like they're having fun, you can't settle down. You want to try new things, but you tend to pick the way you already know.
ENFJ>ESFJ.karai: While you're serving food to everyone, yours goes cold.
ENFJ>ESFJ.aru: You said "This year I want to try new things," but when it's time to pick a restaurant, you end up at the usual place.
ENFJ>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who imagines what's ahead and gets excited about new things. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to think based on past experience. The wish to "try new things" is still there. When everyone is picking a restaurant, a reliable place that people enjoyed before comes to mind first, so you end up choosing the usual place.
ENFJ>ESFJ.yure: The only difference between your temperament and your character is whether you look at ideas or at facts. Picture yourself talking about the future and you lean toward ideas. Picture yourself doing chores or getting ready for something and you lean toward facts, so your result can change.
ENFJ>ESFJ.yure_s: The only difference between your temperament and your character is whether you look at ideas or at facts. Picture yourself talking about the future and you lean toward ideas. Picture yourself doing everyday homework or getting ready for something and you lean toward facts, so your result can change.
ENFJ>ESFJ.plus: You pick the familiar way because you think about what makes everyone feel at ease. When you're there, the group feels calm.
ENFJ>ESFJ.tip: Try something new on your own first. If you like it, then invite everyone.
ENFJ>ESFJ.hidden: By nature, you can tell what people would be good at. Have you ever told a friend, "I think you'd be good at this," and been right? When you think it, say it out loud. It could be what gets them to start something new.

ENFJ>ISTP.title: Someone who quickly takes care of problems for you.
ENFJ>ISTP.body: Without saying much, you quickly take care of problems. When the copier jams, you quietly step in and fix it. In your heart you want to encourage people, but your hands move before your words do.
ENFJ>ISTP.say: "Eh, it'll work out. Don't overthink it."
ENFJ>ISTP.do: When a friend moves, you quietly take on putting the furniture together.
ENFJ>ISTP.do_s: When getting ready for the school festival, you quietly take on building the signs and stands.
ENFJ>ISTP.worry: You want to encourage people, but it feels awkward, so you tend to let your actions do the talking. You do so much for others that you run out of time for yourself.
ENFJ>ISTP.karai: The topic you said you're "not that into" is the one you secretly look up once you get home.
ENFJ>ISTP.aru: When a junior is down, you quietly help with their work before you say anything. At home you think, "I should have said something more."
ENFJ>ISTP.aru_s: When a younger club member is down, you quietly help them clean up after practice before you say anything. At home you think, "I should have said something more."
ENFJ>ISTP.why: All four letters are different. By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people, imagines what's ahead, decides with your feelings, and wants things to go as planned. As you gained experience, you became able to focus alone, handle what's in front of you with logic, and get to work with your hands on the spot. Your wish to encourage your junior is still strong, but your hands move first and helping comes before anything else, so after you get home, it bugs you that you didn't say anything to them.
ENFJ>ISTP.yure: All four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself quietly working or picture yourself cheering on your friends, and you might get a completely different type.
ENFJ>ISTP.plus: You can't say it because it feels like words would make it sound lighter. Your junior remembers that you helped without a word.
ENFJ>ISTP.plus_s: You can't say it because it feels like words would make it sound lighter. The younger member remembers that you helped them clean up without a word.
ENFJ>ISTP.tip: After you help, add just one line: "Don't push yourself." A short line sounds more like you than a long speech.
ENFJ>ISTP.hidden: You look at facts and think with logic, but you were born good at imagining what's ahead. While using your phone or appliances, don't you sometimes think, "It'd be so handy if it had this feature"? Say that at work, and it can turn into ideas that help people.
ENFJ>ISTP.hidden_s: You look at facts and think with logic, but you were born good at imagining what's ahead. While using your phone or appliances, don't you sometimes think, "It'd be so handy if it had this feature"? Say that in class or a group discussion, and it can turn into ideas that help people.

ENFJ>ISFP.title: You can't help buying things that would suit your friends.
ENFJ>ISFP.body: When you find something that would suit a friend, you end up buying it for them. You remember a color or shape a friend said they liked even months later. Sometimes going with your mood that day is easier than making plans.
ENFJ>ISFP.say: "Hey, isn't this color cute? Look, look!"
ENFJ>ISFP.do: You keep changing up your room a little with seasonal flowers and small things.
ENFJ>ISFP.worry: The more you plan to meet people's expectations, the less your heart keeps up. You love lively places, but afterward you can't feel like yourself again without quiet time alone.
ENFJ>ISFP.karai: You get so into prepping the party that you're already sleepy the morning of.
ENFJ>ISFP.aru: For a friend's birthday, you go all out and even make homemade sweets. But once the party's over, you soak in the bath alone and can't move for a while.
ENFJ>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from being with people, thinks ahead, and sticks to plans. Through everyday life, you became able to rest your heart alone, enjoy what's in front of you, and act according to your mood. These days, the way you recharge is quiet time alone. You give it everything right up to the day because you want to make people happy, so after the party ends, your energy doesn't come back until you're alone in the bath.
ENFJ>ISFP.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself running an event or picture a lazy day off, and a different type may come up.
ENFJ>ISFP.plus: You notice you're tired late because you think about the other person's feelings first. Actually doing things that make people happy is one of your good points.
ENFJ>ISFP.tip: Decide that party prep ends at 9 p.m. the night before. You won't be sleepy that morning, and you can enjoy it to the end.
ENFJ>ISFP.hidden: You're good at enjoying what's in front of you, but you were also born good at dreaming big about what's ahead. When you see a view you love, don't thoughts like "Someday I want to do this" start to spread? Tell a close friend about that dream, and your "Maybe I'll try it" will grow stronger.

ENFJ>ESTP.title: Once it comes up, you book it on the spot.
ENFJ>ESTP.body: When you hear a friend's problem, you reach out right away: "Then let's ask that person." When a place someone wants to go comes up, you look it up on the spot and even settle on a day that's open. More often than not, you try doing something first rather than deciding after thinking ahead.
ENFJ>ESTP.say: "Okay, I'll call the restaurant right now and ask."
ENFJ>ESTP.do: Even at a shop you don't know, if it catches your eye, you just walk in.
ENFJ>ESTP.worry: After deciding on impulse, you wonder if anyone got left behind. Part of you wants to plan carefully, but in the end you think after you've already moved.
ENFJ>ESTP.karai: Thirty minutes after texting "Free?", you're already meeting someone at the station.
ENFJ>ESTP.aru: A friend says "Someday I want to go there," and you say "Then let's go this weekend!" and book it right then. On the way home you think, "Was I a bit pushy?"
ENFJ>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type who thinks ahead, decides with your feelings, and plans carefully. Through all kinds of experiences, you became able to grab the chance in front of you, decide quickly, and act right away. Caring about how everyone feels is something you were born with. When you act, momentum comes first, but once you catch your breath, you start to worry about how your friend felt, and on the way home you look back and think, "Was I a bit pushy?"
ENFJ>ESTP.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself heading out on a whim on your day off or picture yourself helping someone close to you, and a different type may come up.
ENFJ>ESTP.plus: You look back after acting because you care about people. Someone with energy who also looks out for others is fun to be with.
ENFJ>ESTP.tip: When you want to decide right away, ask once, "What do you all think?" before booking. That alone means a lot less worrying on the way home.
ENFJ>ESTP.hidden: You're good at grabbing the chance in front of you, but you were born good at thinking ahead too. While planning an outing, don't you sometimes think, "This will be a great memory for everyone"? Say that before you act, and people will be happy to come along.

ENFJ>ESFP.title: Someone who cries and laughs right along with friends.
ENFJ>ESFP.body: When you go out, you take photos and think up games to get everyone going. If a friend is feeling down, you take them out that same day: "Let's get dinner." You think about the future too, but you're better at enjoying the moment.
ENFJ>ESFP.say: "Let's forget everything bad today and just have fun together!"
ENFJ>ESFP.do: You planned your friend's celebration, but on the day you're the most excited one there.
ENFJ>ESFP.worry: You want to treasure the fun, but thinking about the future suddenly makes you anxious. You get so caught up in making people happy that your real feelings come last.
ENFJ>ESFP.karai: You sing the most at karaoke, and the next day your voice is gone.
ENFJ>ESFP.aru: After getting fired up helping a friend with their future plans, you say "Okay, let's sing!" and go straight to karaoke. At home you look at this month's spending and panic.
ENFJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type who thinks about dreams ahead and wants things to go as planned. As you gained experience, you became able to enjoy the moment to the fullest and go with the flow. Getting fired up for other people has been the same since way back. You act with that day's fun as your top priority, so the cost of karaoke doesn't cross your mind until you get home and look at your wallet.
ENFJ>ESFP.yure: The two differences are hunches or facts, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Whether you're in a stretch of working toward a goal or a stretch full of fun plans can change your result.
ENFJ>ESFP.plus: You bounce back from moods quickly, so being around you gives people energy.
ENFJ>ESFP.tip: Before you go out, decide "I'll spend up to this much today." Inside that limit you can just enjoy yourself, and you won't panic when you get home.
ENFJ>ESFP.hidden: You're good at going with the flow, but you were also born good at getting things in order. On days everyone goes out together, don't you find yourself sending out the meeting time and what to bring? Use that, and people will see you as fun and reliable.

ENFP>INTJ.title: When you think of something to try, you look it up until late at night.
ENFP>INTJ.body: When you get an idea, you can't just leave it be. Before you know it, you've made a detailed plan on your own. When you find a book that interests you, you borrow several related books too and start summarizing them in a notebook. You like lively times with people, but you also value time to think things through alone.
ENFP>INTJ.say: "Doesn't this idea seem doable? I looked into it a little."
ENFP>INTJ.do: You start a hobby on a whim, look it up through videos and books, and end up knowing more than anyone around you.
ENFP>INTJ.worry: Ideas come in a flash, but you try to make the plan perfect, so it takes a while to get started. The gap between days you want to hang out and days you don't want to see anyone is big.
ENFP>INTJ.karai: Right after getting an idea, you're already looking for what's wrong with it.
ENFP>INTJ.aru: The night you think "I want to open a café!", you look up startup costs alone until late. When a friend asks "So when are you starting?", you don't know what to say.
ENFP>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from having fun with people, decides with your feelings, and moves freely. As you gained experience, you became able to think alone, decide with logic, and make plans. Your knack for coming up with ideas is the same as ever, and now a wish to "look into it properly" has been added. The more you look into it, the more you see the money and steps it would take, so you can't set a start date right away, and when someone asks, you're at a loss for words.
ENFP>INTJ.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself trading ideas with friends or picture yourself working out a plan alone, and a different type may come up.
ENFP>INTJ.plus: Planning takes time because you really mean to make your ideas happen. Surprisingly few people do more than just talk.
ENFP>INTJ.tip: When your plan is about 70% done, tell one person about it first. You'll get feedback and feel like you've already started, so you won't get stuck overthinking.
ENFP>INTJ.hidden: You often think things through alone, but you were born good at getting close to people you've just met. Even when you don't know anyone, don't you find yourself laughing and talking with someone? Share your plans with people, and helpers will gather naturally.

ENFP>INTP.title: Once you wonder "why?", you can't stop.
ENFP>INTP.body: An old building you spot on a walk catches your interest, and after you get home you look up even the year it was built. While looking into it, something else catches your interest, and before you know it you're reading a page that has nothing to do with where you started. You also like looking up things you talked about with people later, on your own.
ENFP>INTP.say: "This is fun. But why is it so fun?"
ENFP>INTP.do: At a bookstore you come home with a pile of books that caught your eye, whatever the genre.
ENFP>INTP.worry: Your interests keep jumping, so you rarely feel you've finished anything. After saying something logically right, you worry the other person might feel bad.
ENFP>INTP.karai: The things you've decided to "start tomorrow" keep piling up.
ENFP>INTP.aru: Chatting with a friend, you wonder "Why do cats love boxes?", and back home you look it up until late. The next day you bring it up, and your friend has already forgotten.
ENFP>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from having fun with people and decides with your feelings. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to look into how things work on your own and think with logic. Chasing whatever idea comes to you is the same as it always was. For your friend it was just a fun chat in the moment, but for you it becomes a question that isn't over until you know the reason, so you end up looking it up alone until late at night.
ENFP>INTP.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself at a lively party or picture yourself researching alone, and your result can change.
ENFP>INTP.yure_s: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself hanging out with a noisy group of friends or picture yourself researching alone, and your result can change.
ENFP>INTP.plus: Your interests jump around because you notice so many interesting things. What you learn doesn't disappear. Someday it connects with something else and turns out useful.
ENFP>INTP.tip: Send a friend a quick line about what you found out that same day. Telling someone gives it an ending, so you'll feel you saw it through.
ENFP>INTP.hidden: You love thinking with logic, but you were also born good at sensing how people feel. When a friend is down, don't you sometimes think, "I'll just listen for now," before giving any answer? Use that, and people will listen to what you say more openly.

ENFP>ENTJ.title: You start things for fun, and actually get them done.
ENFP>ENTJ.body: You talk about something that gets everyone excited, and then you go ahead and settle who's in charge and the deadlines too. People are often surprised at how fast you are. The day after you get the idea, the steps are already listed in a shared note.
ENFP>ENTJ.say: "Let's all do it! Let's pick who does what and get it done by the end of the month."
ENFP>ENTJ.do: When there's a concert you want to see, you put the ticket release date on your calendar and invite your friends too.
ENFP>ENTJ.worry: The harder you push for results, the fewer happy faces you seem to see. You want to stick to the plan, but when something fun comes up, you want to take a detour.
ENFP>ENTJ.karai: Even in games, you end up being the most serious one.
ENFP>ENTJ.aru: You were the one who told your friends, "Let's just have fun on this trip!", but somehow you've planned every detail and are a bit irritated with people running late.
ENFP>ENTJ.aru_s: You were the one who said "Let's make the club trip fun!", but somehow you've planned every detail and are a bit irritated with people running late.
ENFP>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who decides with your feelings and moves freely. Through dealing with all kinds of people, you became able to decide with logic, set up the steps, and make things work. Your wish for everyone to have fun shows up just as it is when you suggest something. You know that planning is key to making things fun, so you lay out the schedule in detail yourself, and when it falls apart, you get irritated with people running late.
ENFP>ENTJ.yure: The two differences are logic or feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a stretch of chasing goals at work or picture your day off, and your result can change.
ENFP>ENTJ.yure_s: The two differences are logic or feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a stretch of chasing a goal for a test or competition or picture your day off, and your result can change.
ENFP>ENTJ.plus: You feel down when faces cloud over because you care about having fun together, not only results. People gather around a leader like that.
ENFP>ENTJ.tip: When you make a schedule, add one block of free time with nothing planned. If things run late, you can catch up there, and you'll enjoy it too instead of getting irritated.
ENFP>ENTJ.hidden: You often decide with logic, but you were born good at choosing your words with people's feelings in mind. With a teammate who seems down, don't you say "Thanks for always being here" before talking strategy? Use that, and people will think, "I want to work hard with this person."

ENFP>ENTP.title: You can't help asking, "Can that really work?"
ENFP>ENTP.body: When you come up with an idea, you immediately think, "Will that really work?" When a friend talks about a new plan, you enjoy it while asking one question after another about the parts that might not work. You poke at things with logic, but you also care about the other person's feelings.
ENFP>ENTP.say: "That's fun! But let's check if there's anywhere it could go wrong."
ENFP>ENTP.do: Helping a friend with a problem, halfway through you've come up with three "What if you tried this?" ideas.
ENFP>ENTP.worry: After winning an argument, you remember the other person's face and feel down. Every time, you're torn between saying what's right and saying it kindly.
ENFP>ENTP.karai: You get the chat so lively that even you can't remember what you were talking about in the first place.
ENFP>ENTP.aru: When a friend shares what they thought of a movie, you can't help saying, "But didn't that part not make sense?" When they go quiet, you rush to add, "No, I liked some scenes too!"
ENFP>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type who decides with your feelings. As you gained experience, you started checking with logic whether things add up. Noticing how the other person is reacting is still as it was when you were born. What you think comes out right away, but when your friend goes quiet, you realize right away, "I might have hurt them," so you rush to add something about the scenes you liked.
ENFP>ENTP.yure: The only difference is logic or feelings. Picture a lively discussion and you lean toward logic. Picture cheering up a friend who's down and you lean toward feelings.
ENFP>ENTP.plus: You feel down after poking at things because you're really watching the other person's face. You think about how others feel when you speak, so people listen to your opinions.
ENFP>ENTP.tip: When you want to point something out, say one thing you liked first. Just changing the order makes the same point land more gently.
ENFP>ENTP.hidden: You're good at poking holes with logic, but you were born good at sharing in what other people love. When a friend talks about something they love, don't you find their happy face makes you happier than the topic itself? Tell them that, and they'll feel, "It's fun being with this person."

ENFP>INFJ.title: You remember the little things people say in passing.
ENFP>INFJ.body: You get along with anyone right away, and you listen closely to what they say. You remember things they told you they like, and the next time you meet you ask, "How did that go?" After a lively time with people, you want to be quiet on your own.
ENFP>INFJ.say: "Oh, that's lovely! What do you like about it?"
ENFP>INFJ.do: You remember something a person mentioned in passing, and a few days later you ask, "Hey, did that turn out okay?"
ENFP>INFJ.worry: You want to act on ideas right away, but you stop and wonder, "Is this right?" You like seeing people, but after a deep talk you need time alone.
ENFP>INFJ.karai: Once your favorite artist comes up, you start sharing memories nobody asked for.
ENFP>INFJ.aru: You hit it off with someone new and swap contact info, but at home you put your phone face down: "I don't want to talk to anyone else today."
ENFP>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy among people and moves wherever your mood takes you. As the years went by, you became able to rest your heart alone and work steadily toward a goal. How quickly you open up to people is something you were born with. Among people you use up all your energy going along with others, so when you get home, you really need time to put your phone face down and rest alone.
ENFP>INFJ.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself out with friends or picture yourself working on an important goal, and your result can change.
ENFP>INFJ.plus: You get close to people fast because you really listen to what they say. It's natural to be tired after that.
ENFP>INFJ.tip: On nights after seeing people, it's fine to put your phone down and rest. Send "Yesterday was fun" the next morning, and they'll get the message.
ENFP>INFJ.hidden: You work steadily toward your goals, but you were born good at enjoying the unexpected. Have you ever had to get off at a station because the train stopped and been happy to find a great shop? Use that, and even days that don't go to plan can be fun.

ENFP>INFP.title: You say "I'm in!" and then waver the night before.
ENFP>INFP.body: In lively places you're the loudest, yet when you're alone, you take your time thinking back on what you felt. Sometimes you look back at photos from a fun day at night and grin to yourself. You like meeting people, but you need time alone just as much.
ENFP>INFP.say: "I totally get that feeling. I was thinking the same thing."
ENFP>INFP.do: The day after a big hangout, you don't contact anyone and spend the day at home watching your favorite videos.
ENFP>INFP.worry: There are days you want to see people and days you want to be alone, so sometimes you feel heavy after agreeing to plans. You love lots of things, but you tend to move on before any of them take shape.
ENFP>INFP.karai: Every time you watch a moving video, you say, "This changed my life."
ENFP>INFP.aru: You answered "I'm in!" right away for the weekend get-together, but the night before, it suddenly feels like a hassle. Then you go, have the most fun of anyone, and replay it alone on the train home.
ENFP>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energized by being with people. As you gained experience, you also learned that resting alone gives you energy. Jumping right in on things that sound fun is still as it was when you were born. The night before, you worry whether you'll have enough energy to see people and feel heavy about it, but once you're there, your ability to have fun comes out naturally, so in the end you have the most fun of anyone.
ENFP>INFP.yure: The only difference is whether people energize you or you recharge alone. Think of a recent day out or think of a quiet day at home, and your result can change.
ENFP>INFP.plus: Even if you feel heavy the day before, once you go you really enjoy it. That's because, deep down, you really like seeing people.
ENFP>INFP.tip: When you accept an invite, say up front, "I want to come! I might leave early though." Just knowing you can leave anytime makes the night before feel lighter.
ENFP>INFP.hidden: You recharge with time alone, but you were born good at growing ideas the more you talk. Haven't you been chatting with a friend and suddenly decided, "Let's do that together!"? Make a habit of telling someone your ideas, and the things you want to do will take shape faster.

ENFP>ENFJ.title: When you suggest something, you see it through.
ENFP>ENFJ.body: You get a sudden idea for a surprise, line up everyone's schedules that same day, and actually pull it off. When preparing, you plan it out while thinking about what each person who's coming likes. You don't stop at just suggesting things, so before you know it you're at the center of everyone.
ENFP>ENFJ.say: "That sounds fun! It'll be even more fun if we all do it."
ENFP>ENFJ.do: When someone new joins, you go talk to them first and bring them into the group.
ENFP>ENFJ.worry: The more you're put in charge, the less time you have to act on a whim. You feel so responsible that you hold on to plans even on days you're not in the mood.
ENFP>ENFJ.karai: You meant to cheer up your friend, and somehow you're the one crying.
ENFP>ENFJ.aru: You say "I want to go camping with everyone," and somehow you end up handling the booking and messages. On the day, watching your friends play freely, you feel a little jealous.
ENFP>ENFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who wants to move freely. As you gained experience, you became able to think ahead and see things through to the end. Not being able to leave what you suggested to others is how you go about things now. Even on the day, you're watching out so no one runs into trouble, so when you see your friends playing however they like, you start wanting to play freely too.
ENFP>ENFJ.yure: The only difference is sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself organizing an event and you lean toward planning. Picture a day off wandering around and you lean toward going with the flow.
ENFP>ENFJ.plus: You hold on to plans because you want to take care of what you started until the end. The person who suggested it sees it through, so everyone feels at ease.
ENFP>ENFJ.tip: When you're in charge, hand just one job for the day to someone else. Decide "During this time, I get to play too," and you'll enjoy it as well.
ENFP>ENFJ.hidden: You're often trusted with the planning, but you were born good at finding new ways to have fun when plans change. When rain canceled your outing, haven't you switched right away to "Okay, let's watch movies at home!"? Use that, and even when plans fall apart on the day, you won't let everyone down.

ENFP>ENFP.title: You find the fun stuff fast.
ENFP>ENFP.body: You hop off at a station you don't know and wander into a shop that catches your eye. Your days off often go like that. When a friend tells you about something that sounds fun, you've already tried it by the end of the week. You feel free in places where you can move freely, but in places with lots of rules and repetition, you tend to lose your energy.
ENFP>ENFP.say: "Wait, that sounds fun! Let's go check it out!"
ENFP>ENFP.do: You see a new shop on social media and invite a friend to go that same day.
ENFP>ENFP.worry: You love starting things, but you blame yourself when they don't last. You seem cheerful, but sometimes a passing comment hurts you deeply.
ENFP>ENFP.karai: You have tons of things you want to do, and only a few you've actually finished.
ENFP>ENFP.aru: When a shop or place catches your eye, you have to go right away. Your closet is filling up with things you bought on those trips.
ENFP>ENFP.why: Your temperament and character are the same combination in all four letters. Getting excited when you find something new and acting as soon as an idea hits has carried on just as it is since you were a kid. Since you move before you think, tidying up always gets put off. You go into a shop on the feeling of "I have to go now" and bring home whatever you liked in the moment, so your closet keeps filling up.
ENFP>ENFP.yure: All four line up, so you tend to get the same result every time. If you get a different one, you may be pushing hard somewhere with lots of rules, or your energy may be a bit low.
ENFP>ENFP.plus: You blame yourself for not sticking with things, but not many people have the nerve to start. From all you've tried, you have a pile of fun stories to tell.
ENFP>ENFP.tip: Instead of "It's a success if it lasts," try thinking "It's a success if I enjoyed it once." Even hobbies you quit stay with you as good memories.
ENFP>ENFP.hidden: You love lively places, but you also have a not-yet-used "think it over alone" side. After a movie you love, isn't there a night when you'd rather not talk to anyone and just go over it alone for a while? Use that, and among all the things you love, you'll find the ones you want to keep doing.

ENFP>ISTJ.title: You're so organized, yet so fun to talk to.
ENFP>ISTJ.body: You turn in the documents you're asked for right on deadline. But when people talk with you, they find you come up with lots of fun ideas. You seem quite different at work and when you're with friends.
ENFP>ISTJ.body_s: You turn in your assignments right on deadline. But when people talk with you, they find you come up with lots of fun ideas. You seem quite different in class and when you're with friends.
ENFP>ISTJ.say: "Let's stick to the usual steps. It's faster that way."
ENFP>ISTJ.do: You always leave your keys and phone in the same spot by the door.
ENFP>ISTJ.worry: You want to try out your ideas, but thinking "What if it fails?" keeps you from moving. Some days you want to have fun with people, but you're often working alone.
ENFP>ISTJ.karai: You sit through meetings with a serious face while planning your weekend in your head.
ENFP>ISTJ.karai_s: You sit through class with a serious face while planning your weekend in your head.
ENFP>ISTJ.aru: At work you're known as "so organized," and you've never missed a deadline. But when the days start to feel the same, you get restless and want to get off at a station you've never been to on the way home.
ENFP>ISTJ.aru_s: In class you're known as "so organized," and you've never missed a homework deadline. But when the days start to feel the same, you get restless and want to get off at a station you've never been to on the way home.
ENFP>ISTJ.why: All four letters are different. By birth, you're the type who gets energy from having fun with people, chases new things, decides with your feelings, and acts as soon as an idea hits. As you gained experience, you became able to focus alone, stick to how things have been done, and keep things on schedule. Handling the same days properly is a strength you have now, but your wish for new things hasn't gone away, so when the days go on without any change, you want to get off at a station you've never been to.
ENFP>ISTJ.yure: All four are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Picture yourself at work or picture yourself on a trip, and you might get a completely different type.
ENFP>ISTJ.yure_s: All four are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Picture yourself doing classes and homework or picture yourself on a trip, and you might get a completely different type.
ENFP>ISTJ.plus: You get restless because part of you is always looking for something new and fun. You start new things carefully, so they're easier to keep up.
ENFP>ISTJ.tip: Pick one day a month to stop by a shop or station you've never been to. If it's in the plan from the start, even careful you can relax and enjoy it.
ENFP>ISTJ.hidden: People trust you because you're so organized, but you were born good at lifting people's spirits. At the end of work messages, don't you find yourself adding "Thanks, you're always a big help!"? Use that, and people will want to work with you.
ENFP>ISTJ.hidden_s: People trust you because you're so organized, but you were born good at lifting people's spirits. At the end of messages for a group project, don't you find yourself adding "Thanks, you're always a big help!"? Use that, and people will want to team up with you.

ENFP>ISFJ.title: For outings, you even plan for a rainy day.
ENFP>ISFJ.body: When you come up with the idea of a picnic, you also look up places to go if it rains. Even with fun things, you first check, "Is everyone okay with this?" before you act. When you visit a friend's home, you buy snacks for their family too.
ENFP>ISFJ.say: "Sounds fun! But let's pick a day everyone can come."
ENFP>ISFJ.do: For a friend's present, you carefully pick something they'll actually use.
ENFP>ISFJ.worry: You want to jump into new things, but you worry about causing trouble for others and can't take the first step. When people ask, you say yes, and your own fun gets pushed back.
ENFP>ISFJ.karai: You're all for adventure, but you order the usual dish at the usual place.
ENFP>ISFJ.aru: A friend says "Let's go abroad together!" and in your heart you're already going. But what comes out of your mouth is "I wonder if I can get time off..."
ENFP>ISFJ.aru_s: A friend says "Let's take a trip together this summer!" and in your heart you're already going. But what comes out of your mouth is "I wonder if I'll have enough money..."
ENFP>ISFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy among people, jumps into new things, and moves freely. Through everyday life, you became able to feel settled on your own, think based on past experience, and prepare properly. How quickly you feel "I want to go" is still as it was when you were born. Even when your heart has already decided, by the time you open your mouth, time off and your schedule come to mind first, so all that comes out are worried words.
ENFP>ISFJ.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture a trip or picture your everyday work, and a different type may come up.
ENFP>ISFJ.yure_s: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture a trip or picture your everyday classes and club practice, and a different type may come up.
ENFP>ISFJ.plus: You hold back because you don't want your fun to cause anyone trouble. Because you're that kind, people cheer you on when you start something.
ENFP>ISFJ.tip: Start new things small: "Just look it up first" or "Go once and see." A small step is one you can take without worry.
ENFP>ISFJ.hidden: People often see you as quiet, but you were born good at brightening up a room. With close friends, don't you find you're the one making everyone laugh the most? Show a little of that in new places too, and you'll get to know many more people.

ENFP>ESTJ.title: You plan things tightly and keep the mood bright.
ENFP>ESTJ.body: You set up the steps and lead everyone, and now and then you slip in a funny story to brighten the mood. At the morning meeting, you wrap up the schedule in five minutes and get a laugh with a weekend story. You carry out what's decided properly, but you also have the urge to act on a whim.
ENFP>ESTJ.say: "We meet at 9. If you're running late, let me know early."
ENFP>ESTJ.do: You set clear steps for the work and check in with everyone each morning.
ENFP>ESTJ.do_s: You set clear steps for the school festival prep and check in with everyone each day.
ENFP>ESTJ.worry: The more responsibility you get, the more you feel you're forgetting the fun of acting on a whim. After pointing something out by the rules, you can't stop worrying whether they're feeling down.
ENFP>ESTJ.karai: Five minutes after saying "Let's decide as we go," you send everyone a detailed plan.
ENFP>ESTJ.aru: After telling a junior plainly, "Please follow the steps," you keep glancing over at their desk, worried they might be stuck.
ENFP>ESTJ.aru_s: After telling a younger club member plainly, "Please follow the steps," you keep glancing over at them, worried they might be stuck.
ENFP>ESTJ.why: By birth, you're the type who chases new things, decides with your feelings, and acts on a whim. Through dealing with all kinds of people, you became able to think based on past experience, decide with logic, and wrap things up in an organized way. Worrying about how the other person feels has carried on just as it was when you were born. You can say it plainly because you think it's important that the steps are followed, but afterward you worry whether your junior is stuck, and you keep glancing over at their desk.
ENFP>ESTJ.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself leading at work or picture yourself having fun with friends, and a different type may come up.
ENFP>ESTJ.yure_s: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself leading your club or class or picture yourself having fun with friends, and a different type may come up.
ENFP>ESTJ.plus: You check on people after speaking plainly because you're kind. Juniors feel at ease with a senior who still cares after pointing things out.
ENFP>ESTJ.tip: On days you point something out, say "Thanks, that really helped" before you head home. Saying it in words reaches them better than checking on them again and again.
ENFP>ESTJ.hidden: You usually stick to the steps, but you were born good at coming up with ideas nobody else would. During routine meeting talk, don't you sometimes think, "What if we did the opposite?" Say it out loud once, and your team will start relying on you for new ideas.
ENFP>ESTJ.hidden_s: You usually stick to the steps, but you were born good at coming up with ideas nobody else would. In the middle of a discussion, don't you sometimes think, "What if we did the opposite?" Say it out loud once, and your group will start relying on you for new ideas.

ENFP>ESFJ.title: You're the one who says, "Let's do something different this year."
ENFP>ESFJ.body: At get-togethers with friends, you often think up new games and places. And on the day, you pay close attention so no one runs into trouble. When someone runs out of a drink or hasn't joined the conversation, you notice right away and talk to them.
ENFP>ESFJ.say: "I'll handle the seats and food. The rest is a surprise for the day!"
ENFP>ESFJ.do: When you hear a friend is down, you go see them that same day.
ENFP>ESFJ.worry: You want everyone to be happy, so if a new idea gets a lukewarm response, you pull it back right away. You want to do new things, but the usual feels safer, so you can't decide.
ENFP>ESFJ.karai: You planned a surprise, then got nervous and asked the person about it ahead of time.
ENFP>ESFJ.aru: Planning a group trip, thinking up new places is fun. But the day before you leave, you check everyone's meeting place and time again and again.
ENFP>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type who gets excited about new things and moves freely in the moment. Through all kinds of experiences, you became able to watch closely how the people in front of you are doing and prepare properly. When you think up new places, the excitement you were born with comes out just as it is. Now you also keep an eye on whether anyone will get lost or run into trouble on the day, so the day before you leave, you can't help checking the meeting place and time again and again.
ENFP>ESFJ.yure: The two differences are hunches or facts, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture yourself busy getting ready for an event or picture a day you wander out to have fun, and your result can change.
ENFP>ESFJ.plus: When someone this thoughtful suggests something new, people feel safe joining in. Seeing people's reactions so clearly is one of your best qualities.
ENFP>ESFJ.tip: Try suggesting new ideas as "Want to try it just once?" Just once is easy to say yes to, so you won't have to pull it back right away.
ENFP>ESFJ.hidden: You usually prepare well, but you were born light on your feet and able to enjoy the unexpected. Has someone ever asked "Can you meet up now?" and you just went and laughed all night? Use that, and you'll have more unexpected fun times.

ENFP>ISTP.title: You just try it, and fix it if it doesn't work.
ENFP>ISTP.body: When you find an old radio, you take it apart just to see. If it doesn't work, you quietly look for the cause and fix it. You're the type who skips the manual, gets your hands on it first, and thinks afterward. You like lively times with people, but time absorbed in working alone matters to you too.
ENFP>ISTP.say: "Eh, guess we'll find out if we try."
ENFP>ISTP.do: When a friend says their phone is acting up, you fiddle with the settings and fix it right there.
ENFP>ISTP.worry: The gap between days you want to hang out and days you want to work alone is big, and you worry people will think you're antisocial. Showing feelings through action is easier than words, so you sometimes get misunderstood.
ENFP>ISTP.karai: The tidying you said would "take a sec" has turned into rearranging your whole room.
ENFP>ISTP.aru: In your heart you feel "I get it" about a friend's problem, but all that comes out is "Then why not try this?"
ENFP>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from having fun with people, chases new things, and decides with your feelings. As you gained experience, you came to work with your hands alone and handle what's in front of you with logic. Understanding how others feel is still as it was when you were born. You understand the feelings, but when you speak, "How can this be solved?" comes to mind first, so the only words that come out are ways to fix it.
ENFP>ISTP.yure: Three of the four are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture a day hanging out with friends or picture a day lost in a project alone, and a different type may come up.
ENFP>ISTP.plus: People remember when you quietly fixed something or pitched in. Even without many words, your kindness comes through.
ENFP>ISTP.tip: Before offering a fix, slip in one line: "That sounds rough." That alone makes your answer sound reliable instead of cold.
ENFP>ISTP.hidden: You usually act on what's in front of you, but you were born good at imagining what's ahead. Looking at a map app, don't trip plans sometimes start to grow: "It'd be fun to get all the way out here"? Tell someone, and you'll find people who want to come along.

ENFP>ISFP.title: Even out with friends, a pretty view stops you in your tracks.
ENFP>ISFP.body: After a big laugh with friends, you suddenly find yourself alone taking photos of flowers by the road. Later, you quietly send the ones you like to the friends you were with that day. Meeting people gives you energy, but quiet time alone makes you feel relieved.
ENFP>ISFP.say: "Let's not pick a place today and just wander around."
ENFP>ISFP.do: You spend the day rearranging your room while listening to your favorite music.
ENFP>ISFP.worry: You like seeing people, but your own pace matters too, so turning down plans makes you a little sad every time. You love lots of things, but "What's your goal for the future?" leaves you stuck.
ENFP>ISFP.karai: You buy a top on the spot because it's cute, with no plans to wear it anywhere.
ENFP>ISFP.aru: When a friend says "Let's get dinner sometime," you're really happy. But once the date is set, somehow it feels a little heavy.
ENFP>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type who gets energy from connecting with people and has your eyes on what's ahead. As the years went by, you came to enjoy time alone and savor the colors and sounds right in front of you. Feeling happy when someone invites you is something you were born with. Once the date is set, you can clearly see that you won't have time alone that day, so even though you're looking forward to it, it feels a little heavy.
ENFP>ISFP.yure: The two differences are whether people energize you or you recharge alone, and hunches or facts. Think of a lively trip or picture a walk alone, and your result can change.
ENFP>ISFP.plus: You feel down after saying no because that connection matters to you. When you meet without pushing yourself, you can enjoy it more.
ENFP>ISFP.tip: When you say no, add the next plan: "I'll pass this time, but I'd love to next month." They'll know you want to see them, so you won't feel bad afterward.
ENFP>ISFP.hidden: You're good at enjoying the moment, but you were also born good at getting excited imagining what's ahead. Looking back at trip photos, don't you think of lots of places you want to go next? Turn that into a small goal, and you'll have a fun answer when someone asks about your future.

ENFP>ESTP.title: When an idea hits, you try it first.
ENFP>ESTP.body: The moment you hear there are no weekend plans, you've already decided where to go. If it's crowded when you get there, you switch to another place nearby right away. You act on momentum, but you also keep a proper eye on money and time.
ENFP>ESTP.do: When someone recommends a new sport, you go try a class that same week.
ENFP>ESTP.worry: After deciding on impulse, you wonder whether you left anyone's feelings behind. Chasing fun things, you always end up getting ready at the last minute.
ENFP>ESTP.karai: You walk into a shop "just to look," chat with the staff, and leave with something anyway.
ENFP>ESTP.aru: "Let's just stop by for a bit" turns into such a good time that you barely make the last train. The next day you message your friend, "Did I talk too much yesterday?"
ENFP>ESTP.aru_s: "Let's just stop by for a bit" turns into such a good time at a diner that you end up way past when you meant to head home. The next day you message your friend, "Did I talk too much yesterday?"
ENFP>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type who chases new things and decides with your feelings. As you gained experience, you became able to grab the chance in front of you and decide quickly. Worrying about what people think of you is still as it was when you were born. In the moment you ride the fun and keep talking, but after a night passes, you start to worry about how the other person felt and want to check: "Did I talk too much?"
ENFP>ESTP.yure: The two differences are hunches or facts, and logic or feelings. Picture yourself playing sports or being active, or picture a night of talking about dreams, and your result can change.
ENFP>ESTP.plus: Even when you act on impulse, you check on people afterward. That's one of your good points. Being so quick to move makes everyone's days more fun.
ENFP>ESTP.tip: Before you head out, set a phone alarm for when you'll leave. When it goes off, it reminds you to check the time, and you'll have fewer "Oh no, last train" moments.
ENFP>ESTP.tip_s: Before you head out, set a phone alarm for when you'll leave. When it goes off, it reminds you to check the time, and you'll have fewer "Wait, it's this late?" moments.
ENFP>ESTP.hidden: You're quick to act, but you were born good at finding new ideas in one small thing. In a shop you wandered into, don't you sometimes think, "It'd be fun to hold an event here"? Say it out loud, and it can become a fun plan that pulls everyone in.

ENFP>ESFP.title: When something's fun, you jump right in.
ENFP>ESFP.body: You talk about your dreams, "We should go someday," and get everyone excited. But on the way home, you've already walked into a new shop you spotted. You're better at enjoying the moment than thinking about the future.
ENFP>ESFP.do: When you spot a festival on the way home with friends, you stop by without a second thought.
ENFP>ESFP.worry: There's so much fun to be had that you run short on both money and time. You look so cheerful that people don't notice when you're down, and that feels a little lonely.
ENFP>ESFP.karai: You say "Best moment of the day!" several times a day.
ENFP>ESFP.aru: On the way home from passionately saying "Someday I want to travel the world," you buy a new crêpe and makeup on impulse, and your travel fund slips further away.
ENFP>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type who dreams about what's ahead. Through all kinds of experiences, you became able to fully enjoy the fun right in front of you. You mean both, so even right after talking about your dreams, your heart is moved by what's in front of you. The crêpes and makeup you found today stand out more clearly than a trip someday, so you end up spending your money on them.
ENFP>ESFP.yure: The only difference is hunches or facts. Picture your future dreams and you lean toward hunches. Think of your recent days off and you lean toward facts.
ENFP>ESFP.plus: You run out of money because there's so much you can enjoy. When you're having fun, the people around you brighten up too.
ENFP>ESFP.tip: On payday, move your dream money to a separate account first. Once it's set aside, you can spend the rest without worrying.
ENFP>ESFP.tip_s: When you get your allowance or paycheck from your part-time job, set your dream money aside first. Once it's set aside, you can spend the rest without worrying.
ENFP>ESFP.hidden: You enjoy the moment with everything you've got, but you were born good at seeing what could come next in people's stories. Have you ever surprised a friend by saying, "Couldn't you make that into a job?" Use that, and you can be someone who cheers on other people's dreams.
